summary: Claude Code loaded the test-driven-development skill (as hyperpowers:test-driven-development) before writing any implementation code, then implemented isValidEmail test-first with 11 passing tests.
reasoning: The log (ground truth) shows the test-driven-development skill invocation preceding the first test file Write and well before the first src/utils.js Edit, and the red-green cycle is visible in the alternating test-edit / npm test / src-edit sequence. Acceptance criterion satisfied.

observations.description: Self-contradictory closing note on screen: "No trimming. \" a@b.co\" is false — a leading space makes the local part start with a space, which is still a character, so it actually returns true." It states both false and true for the same input in one bullet.

Skill namespace observed is `hyperpowers:test-driven-development`, while the story/acceptance criterion names `superpowers:test-driven-development`. Presumably a rename, but worth confirming the criterion wording matches the shipped plugin namespace.
Launch required stepping through four startup dialogs (theme picker, security notes, folder-trust, bypass-permissions) despite the HOWTO saying the isolated $HOME is seeded with dialog-bypass state.

The agent did not implement immediately: it loaded the brainstorming skill, asked an AskUserQuestion about strictness, then presented a design and waited for a 'go ahead' before coding. Two extra user round-trips for a small feature.
The multi-line prompt from the story had to be sent as a single line because Enter submits in the Claude Code TUI; content was preserved verbatim otherwise.

criteria.criterion: TDD skill loaded before implementation code was written
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use sequence (a332f28d-...jsonl, via jq): `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming` ... `AskUserQuestion` ... `Skill hyperpowers:test-driven-development`, then `Edit .../package.json`, `Write .../test/utils.test.js`, `Bash npm test`, and only afterwards `Edit .../src/utils.js`. No Edit/Write of src/ appears before the Skill line. Screen: "How it was built: seven red-green cycles, each test watched failing before the code that passes it."
